messages.subject: sampling effort / multiplier
parts:
Hello,

I am doing my Master thesis in dry forest of Peru estimating density of white tailed dear in a protected area. We have 6 transects that are annually surveyed 6 or 7 days. Each day transects are visited twice in the morning and in the afternoon. 

In five years of analysis, some years there are exceptions when one transect was surveyed 5 days instead of 6 days or maybe they were surveyed 6 days but one of those days it was visited in the morning and not in the afternoon.

In the entry format to distance I have 5 columns, one being transect length, I don´t understand how to explain to distance that the transects are being surveyed 6 or 7 seven days two times a day. Should I do this as a multiplier and how to do it or should I multiply the transect length for the number of times that was visited (6 transects*2 times /day* Num.days). I have always understand that transect lengh in the data entry wizard is just the length so I don´t understand where can I specify the sampling effort and tell distance that the 300 observations I have for a certain year correspond to 12 visits (number of days * 2 visits per day).

Thank you for your help,

Laura

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] sampling effort / multiplier
parts:
Laura:

The easiest way to remember how to provide information to Distance about your survey is that you are describing the amount of effort associated with your survey.  One of the fundamental pieces of information needed for density estimation is the "encounter rate", which for line transects is the number of objects detected per metre (or kilometre) of effort.

Therefore, in your situation, effort is the length of the transect multiplied by the number of times the transect is walked.  That is the value you should provide to Distance when asked to provide line length for each transect.  You could do this as a multiplier, but only if all transects are visited the same number of times (because multipliers can only be applied for the entire study area).  Because your number of visits is not constant, your best solution is to enter line length times number of visits in the "effort" column.

As an aside, note that having 6 transects will make it difficult for you to obtain a good estimate of the variability in encounter rate between transects.  In the future, your study would be improved by increasing the number of transects in your study; both to improve the estimate of variability in encounter rate and to broaden the representativeness of your transects to the study area.

I will answer your second question (about clusters) separately so that the email thread is maintained.

messages.author: 2406e2a7a3277f65
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] sampling effort / multiplier
parts:
Thank you Eric. 
Very helpful. I have now correct the transect length column with total distance travelled throughout the survey for each transect.

Yes, I understand having 6 transects is not good practice, we have increased this to 8 since 2010. This is a very steep and hot site not easy to work in and we don´t have enough budget to increase to 10-20 as recommended. I hope I can state this clear enough in my thesis so that its considered an increase in budget.

Best,
Laura
